sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: To be human, to be alive, is to be vulnerable to sadness and suffering.
sentences.zh: 身为人类，活着，就意味着容易受到悲伤和痛苦的侵袭。

sentences.en: For centuries, artists, writers, and thinkers have tried to capture what this feels like.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，艺术家、作家和思想家们一直试图捕捉这种感受。

sentences.en: The author William Styron once said,
sentences.zh: 作家威廉·斯泰伦曾说，

sentences.en: the great drizzle of horror induced by depression takes on the quality of physical pain.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症带来的那种巨大的恐怖细雨，带有一种生理痛苦的特质。

sentences.en: But it is not an immediately identifiable pain like that of a broken limb.
sentences.zh: 但它不像骨折那样，是一种能立刻辨认出来的疼痛。

sentences.en: It may be more accurate to say that despair comes to resemble the diabolical discomfort
sentences.zh: 或许更准确地说，绝望就像是一种恶魔般的折磨，

sentences.en: of being imprisoned in a fiercely overheated room.
sentences.zh: 仿佛被囚禁在一间酷热难耐的房间里。

sentences.en: And because no breeze stirs this cauldron,
sentences.zh: 因为没有一丝微风能搅动这口大锅，

sentences.en: because there is no escape from the smothering confinement,
sentences.zh: 因为无法逃离这种令人窒息的禁锢，

sentences.en: it is entirely natural that the victim begins to think ceaselessly of oblivion.
sentences.zh: 受害者开始不断地想到遗忘，这完全是自然而然的。

sentences.en: Sometimes our suffering is connected to what we see in the world.
sentences.zh: 有时我们的痛苦与我们眼中的世界有关。

sentences.en: During the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln, who was already prone to depression,
sentences.zh: 内战期间，亚伯拉罕·林肯总统，他本就容易抑郁，

sentences.en: was often consumed by the horrors of the war.
sentences.zh: 常常被战争的恐怖所吞噬。

sentences.en: His secretary, John Hay, would note that
sentences.zh: 他的秘书约翰·海曾记录道，

sentences.en: he would sit for hours staring vacantly out the window,
sentences.zh: 他会一连几个小时呆滞地望着窗外，

sentences.en: his face displaying the deepest sorrow imaginable.
sentences.zh: 脸上流露出难以想象的深切悲哀。

sentences.en: But as long as humans have been suffering,
sentences.zh: 但只要人类还在遭受痛苦，

sentences.en: humans have also been trying to find paths out of suffering.
sentences.zh: 人类也一直在寻找走出痛苦的途径。

sentences.en: Philosophers, scientists, and spiritual leaders
sentences.zh: 哲学家、科学家和精神领袖们

sentences.en: have offered many ideas on how to live a life of contentment.
sentences.zh: 为如何过上知足的生活提供了许多见解。

sentences.en: Today on the show, we explore the ideas of an unusual philosopher king who lived some 19 centuries ago.
sentences.zh: 今天节目中，我们将探讨一位生活在约19个世纪前、不同寻常的“哲学家国王”的思想。

sentences.en: There's a reason his meditations about a life worth living have survived nearly 2,000 years.
sentences.zh: 他关于值得过的人生所写的沉思录能流传近两千年，是有原因的。

sentences.en: Ancient ideas to help us find a way out of modern despondencies.
sentences.zh: 用古老的智慧帮助我们找到摆脱现代忧郁的方法。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Most of us have been there.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都经历过这种情况。

sentences.en: Low points in our life when we look around and realize that something needs to change.
sentences.zh: 在我们人生的低谷期，环顾四周，意识到有些事情必须改变。

sentences.en: What we do in these moments can spell the difference between a life of well-being or a life of despair.
sentences.zh: 在这些时刻我们所做的事情，决定了我们是过上幸福的生活，还是陷入绝望的深渊。

sentences.en: At the City College of New York, philosopher Massimo Piliucci has personal experience with such moments in his own life.
sentences.zh: 在纽约城市学院，哲学家马西莫·皮利乌奇对这种人生时刻有着亲身体会。

sentences.en: Massimo Piliucci, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 马西莫·皮利乌奇，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Massimo, your world fell apart when you turned 40.
sentences.zh: 马西莫，你40岁时，你的世界崩塌了。

sentences.en: Where were you living at the time?
sentences.zh: 那时你住在哪里？

sentences.en: I was in Knoxville, Tennessee, the buckle of the Bible belt, as they call it.
sentences.zh: 我当时在田纳西州的诺克斯维尔，也就是人们所说的“圣经带”的核心地带。

sentences.en: And what was going on in your life?
sentences.zh: 那时你的生活发生了什么？

sentences.en: I had started my academic career at the University of Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 我当时刚在田纳西大学开始我的学术生涯。

sentences.en: I was a biologist at the time, not a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 那时我是一名生物学家，还不是哲学家。

sentences.en: And I was being treated very well by the university there.
sentences.zh: 大学对我非常优待。

sentences.en: But at the same time, there were a couple of things that were problematic.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，有几件事让我感到困扰。

sentences.en: Number one, the local culture was difficult for me to live in.
sentences.zh: 第一，当地的文化让我很难适应。

sentences.en: I was a professor of evolutionary biology.
sentences.zh: 我是一名进化生物学教授。

sentences.en: My students, some of them actually told me that I was probably going to go to hell.
sentences.zh: 我的学生，有些人甚至告诉我，我可能会下地狱。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, that's shamanji.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这真是太荒谬了。

sentences.en: But the more important bit was that I had a daughter from a previous relationship, and she was living on the East Coast in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的一点是，我与前任有一个女儿，她住在东海岸的康涅狄格州。

sentences.en: So I always wanted to move back into that area.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直想搬回那个地区。

sentences.en: And that is problematic for somebody who is a full professor with tenure because there are very few positions available, especially in the East Coast,
sentences.zh: 对于一位拥有终身教职的正教授来说，这很困难，因为职位非常少，尤其是在东海岸，

sentences.en: because everybody wants to go there.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都想去那里。

sentences.en: and typically universities hire junior faculty, not senior professionals.
sentences.zh: 而且通常大学倾向于聘请初级教员，而不是资深专家。

sentences.en: So that was a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个问题。

sentences.en: Massimo tried to address the situation by applying for jobs on the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 马西莫试图通过申请东海岸的工作来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: As luck would have it, he landed a position with Stony Brook University on Long Island.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他在长岛的石溪大学获得了一个职位。

sentences.en: But even as it seemed like a solution was at hand for one challenge, others cropped up.
sentences.zh: 但就在一个挑战似乎即将解决时，其他问题又接踵而至。

sentences.en: Massimo and his wife started having problems in their marriage.
sentences.zh: 马西莫和他的妻子婚姻出现了问题。

sentences.en: Instead of moving together to Long Island, they decided to get a divorce.
sentences.zh: 他们决定离婚，而不是一起搬到长岛。

sentences.en: And then Massimo's father, who lived thousands of miles away, was diagnosed with cancer.
sentences.zh: 接着，远在千里之外的马西莫的父亲被诊断出患有癌症。

sentences.en: So my father had been hit by multiple types of cancer.
sentences.zh: 我父亲患上了多种癌症。

sentences.en: He was a big smoker.
sentences.zh: 他是个老烟枪。

sentences.en: So at that point, my mother, his ex-wife, made a comment.
sentences.zh: 当时，我母亲，也就是他的前妻，评论了一句。

sentences.en: He said, l'erba cativa non more mai, which is Italian for the bad weeds never die.
sentences.zh: 她说：“L'erba cattiva non muore mai”，这是意大利语，意思是“坏草永远不会死”。

sentences.en: She meant it as a joke, but it was, you know.
sentences.zh: 她是开玩笑说的，但你知道，确实如此。

sentences.en: and then all of a sudden things took a turn for the worse and it killed him in a matter of weeks
sentences.zh: 突然间情况急转直下，几周内他就去世了。

sentences.en: in fact it was so fast that i did not have the time to really do anything uh you know i was on
sentences.zh: 事实上，一切发生得太快，我根本来不及做任何事，我当时

sentences.en: my way literally on my way to the airport to get on the plane to get to rome and go see him and my
sentences.zh: 正在去机场的路上，准备搭飞机去罗马看他，然后我

sentences.en: brother called me saying you know that just that i literally broke down crying on the highway i had
sentences.zh: 兄弟给我打电话，告诉我这个消息，我在高速公路上崩溃大哭，不得不

sentences.en: to pull over.
sentences.zh: 把车停在路边。

sentences.en: So I was able to get to his funeral, but not being there in the last few moments.
sentences.zh: 所以我赶上了他的葬礼，但没能在他生命的最后时刻陪伴他。

sentences.en: So at this point, picture this.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下当时的情况。

sentences.en: In a span of a few months, I got hit with this news that apparently
sentences.zh: 在短短几个月内，我接连收到消息，显然

sentences.en: I'm going to be divorced.
sentences.zh: 我要离婚了。

sentences.en: My father dies.
sentences.zh: 我父亲去世了。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, of course, I had accepted the
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当然，我已经接受了

sentences.en: position at Stony Brook, which meant that I had a new job.
sentences.zh: 石溪大学的职位，这意味着我有一份新工作。

sentences.en: I had to move across the country and I
sentences.zh: 我必须搬到全国的另一端，而且

sentences.en: had to find a new house.
sentences.zh: 我必须找一栋新房子。

sentences.en: Now, any psychologist worth its salt would tell you that one or two
sentences.zh: 任何称职的心理学家都会告诉你，其中一两件事

sentences.en: of those things is pretty stressful.
sentences.zh: 就足以让人压力巨大。

sentences.en: Four or five of them simultaneously, that's a lot.
sentences.zh: 同时发生四五件事，那真是太沉重了。

sentences.en: So during this time of upheaval in your life, you found consolation and guidance in an unexpected
sentences.zh: 那么在你人生的这段动荡时期，你在一个意想不到的

sentences.en: source.
sentences.zh: 来源中找到了慰藉和指引。

sentences.en: It was a book you had encountered many years earlier in college, but rereading it this
sentences.zh: 那是一本你在大学时就接触过的书，但这次重读，

sentences.en: time, you felt like it was speaking directly to you.
sentences.zh: 你感觉它仿佛在直接与你对话。

sentences.en: What was this book, Massimo?
sentences.zh: 那是什么书，马西莫？

sentences.en: The book was
sentences.zh: 那本书是

sentences.en: The Meditations by Marcus Aurelius, which is a stoic book.
sentences.zh: 马可·奥勒留的《沉思录》，这是一本斯多葛派的书。

sentences.en: And that's interesting in itself,
sentences.zh: 这本身就很有趣，

sentences.en: because the first time that I came across Marcus Aurelius, I thought, stoic is, oh, come on,
sentences.zh: 因为我第一次接触马可·奥勒留时，我想，斯多葛派，噢，得了吧，

sentences.en: who wants to live a life like a stoic?
sentences.zh: 谁想过斯多葛派那样的生活？

sentences.en: I mean, aren't these the kind of people that go around
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道他们不是那种整天

sentences.en: with a stiff upper lip and suppressing emotions, right?
sentences.zh: 板着脸、压抑情感的人吗？

sentences.en: So, kind of like Mr. Spock from Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 就像《星际迷航》里的史波克先生那样。

sentences.en: So, when I came across Marcus, again, I thought, hmm, I don't know about this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我再次遇到马可时，我想，嗯，我不确定这东西怎么样。

sentences.en: And then I opened the meditations and one of the first phrases,
sentences.zh: 然后我打开了《沉思录》，其中一句话，

sentences.en: so the meditation is not the kind of book that you necessarily read cover to cover because it was a personal philosophical diary or journal of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 《沉思录》并不是那种你需要从头读到尾的书，因为它是一位皇帝的私人哲学日记或随笔。

sentences.en: So it was not in fact meant for publication.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上并不是为了出版而写的。

sentences.en: So when I opened it up at random, one of the first few sentences that I found is in one of the later books and it said something like,
sentences.zh: 当我随意翻开它时，我发现的头几句话之一是在后面的章节里，它大概是这样说的：

sentences.en: you don't like the cucumber because it's bitter.
sentences.zh: 你不喜欢黄瓜，因为它太苦了。

sentences.en: Well, don't eat it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就别吃它。

sentences.en: Why do you have to go on and complain about the fact that there are bitter cucumbers in the world?
sentences.zh: 为什么还要一直抱怨世界上有苦黄瓜呢？

sentences.en: That struck me as very powerful and very insightful.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得非常有力量，也非常有洞察力。

sentences.en: We tend to complain all the time about the fact that things don't go our way,
sentences.zh: 我们总是倾向于抱怨事情不顺心，

sentences.en: that the world is not the way we would like it to be.
sentences.zh: 抱怨世界不是我们想要的样子。

sentences.en: And those complaints don't do anything practical.
sentences.zh: 而这些抱怨没有任何实际作用。

sentences.en: They're not actionable.
sentences.zh: 它们是无法付诸行动的。

sentences.en: So complaining about it becomes simply a way to wallow in your self-pity or to fuel your own dissatisfaction with the world, which makes the thing worse.
sentences.zh: 所以抱怨只会让你沉溺于自怜，或者加剧你对世界的不满，这只会让事情变得更糟。

sentences.en: So now you have both an external situation, some aspect of the world that you don't like,
sentences.zh: 所以现在你不仅面临一个外部情况，即你不喜欢的世界某一方面，

sentences.en: and you are making yourself inwardly worse by complaining about it in a way that it gets frustrating because you can't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 而且你还通过抱怨让自己内心变得更糟，这让人感到沮丧，因为你对此无能为力。

sentences.en: So, I went back to that phrase.
sentences.zh: 所以，我回到了那句话。

sentences.en: It says, okay, there are bitter cucumbers in the world.
sentences.zh: 它说，好吧，世界上有苦黄瓜。

sentences.en: That's a fact, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个事实，对吧？

sentences.en: I do not have the power to eliminate bitter cucumbers from the world.
sentences.zh: 我没有能力消除世界上的苦黄瓜。

sentences.en: I do have the power to refuse to eat them.
sentences.zh: 但我有能力拒绝吃它们。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Marcus is absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 马可说得完全正确。

sentences.en: I don't need the additional step of complaining and involving in this fact that the world is so unfair because there are bitter cucumbers.
sentences.zh: 我不需要再多此一举地去抱怨，去纠结于世界因为有苦黄瓜而不公平这个事实。

sentences.en: That was the beginning, or one of the beginnings, because I also got, pretty much at the same time, another stunning phrase from Epictetus, who was one of the inspirations,
sentences.zh: 那是开始，或者说是开始之一，因为我几乎在同一时间，从爱比克泰德那里得到了另一句令人震撼的话，他是灵感来源之一，

sentences.en: to Marcus, so the two are very closely related.
sentences.zh: 对马可来说，所以两者联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: Epictetus was another interesting guy.
sentences.zh: 爱比克泰德是另一个有趣的人。

sentences.en: You know, Marcus Aurelius was an emperor, so literally the most powerful person in the Mediterranean world at the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，马可·奥勒留是一位皇帝，所以他确实是当时地中海世界最有权势的人。

sentences.en: Epictetus was at the opposite extreme.
sentences.zh: 爱比克泰德则处于另一个极端。

sentences.en: He was a slave.
sentences.zh: 他是个奴隶。

sentences.en: He started out life as a slave.
sentences.zh: 他的人生起点是奴隶。

sentences.en: He was actually eventually freed and he became actually one of the most well-known and respected teachers in the Mediterranean era at the beginning of the second century.
sentences.zh: 他最终获得了自由，并成为了二世纪初地中海地区最著名、最受尊敬的老师之一。

sentences.en: So it was a very, you know, had a completely different sort of life trajectory.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他的人生轨迹完全不同。

sentences.en: And yet the ideas, the stoic ideas resonated a panther with both of these people and both of them became major conduits for later generations.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些斯多葛派的思想在两人身上都产生了共鸣，他们两人都成为了后代的重要思想传递者。

sentences.en: And one of the things that Epictetus says at the beginning of the discourses is, so you want to make money.
sentences.zh: 爱比克泰德在《语录》开头说的一件事是：你想赚钱。

sentences.en: He's talking to some of his friends.
sentences.zh: 他是在和他的朋友们交谈。

sentences.en: You want to make money or you want me to make money so that I can help you?
sentences.zh: 你想赚钱，或者你想让我赚钱，这样我就可以帮助你？

sentences.en: Well, that's all fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这都没问题。

sentences.en: But what am I going to do with that money?
sentences.zh: 但我拿这些钱做什么呢？

sentences.en: The money itself isn't going to tell me.
sentences.zh: 钱本身不会告诉我。

sentences.en: What's going to tell me is my faculty of judgment.
sentences.zh: 能告诉我的，是我的判断力。

sentences.en: And Epictetus uses this to make the general stoic point that so-called externals,
sentences.zh: 爱比克泰德用这一点来阐述斯多葛派的普遍观点，即所谓的外部事物，

sentences.en: things like money or health even, or reputation, are not the fundamental thing.
sentences.zh: 像金钱、健康甚至名誉，都不是根本的东西。

sentences.en: They're not crucial because it all depends on how you use them, right?
sentences.zh: 它们并不关键，因为一切都取决于你如何使用它们，对吧？

sentences.en: You can be very rich and do a lot of damage.
sentences.zh: 你可以非常有钱，却造成很多破坏。

sentences.en: Or you may be very poor and actually use your resources very wisely.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能非常贫穷，却能非常明智地利用你的资源。

sentences.en: To Epictetus and Marcus, it's not fame or money or wealth or whatever it is per se.
sentences.zh: 对爱比克泰德和马可来说，名声、金钱、财富或其他任何东西本身并不重要。

sentences.en: It's how you use them that makes a difference.
sentences.zh: 重要的是你如何使用它们，这才是关键。

sentences.en: And that struck me as another fundamental insight from Stoicism, that why are you now
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得这是斯多葛主义的另一个基本洞见，为什么你现在

sentences.en: focusing on improving your decision-making ability and you keep focusing instead on more
sentences.zh: 专注于提高你的决策能力，而你却一直专注于

sentences.en: or less mindlessly follow what society at large tells you, that you're trying to become
sentences.zh: 盲目地追随社会大众告诉你的东西，即你试图变得

sentences.en: more wealthy, more famous, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 更富有、更出名等等。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: What are you going to do with all that stuff once you have it?
sentences.zh: 一旦你拥有了所有这些东西，你打算用它们做什么？

sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨马可·奥勒留的思想如何帮助我们指引方向，度过

sentences.en: the challenges of modern life.
sentences.zh: 现代生活的挑战。

sentences.zh: 当然，我们刚才在谈论我的身体形象问题。

sentences.en: What do you mean my health is not up to me?
sentences.zh: 你说我的健康不是我力所能及的，是什么意思？

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是啊。

sentences.en: I can do all sorts of things about my health, right?
sentences.zh: 我可以在健康方面做各种各样的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: I can eat a good diet.
sentences.zh: 我可以保持良好的饮食。

sentences.en: You know, I can go and exercise.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以去锻炼。

sentences.en: I can go to the doctor on a regular basis and practice preventive medicine.
sentences.zh: 我可以定期去看医生，进行预防性医疗。

sentences.en: I mean, I can do all those.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我能做所有这些事。

sentences.en: But then you think about it and say, ah, but wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但当你仔细思考后会说，啊，等等。

sentences.en: Those are all judgments or decisions to act or not to act.
sentences.zh: 那些都是判断，或是采取行动或不采取行动的决定。

sentences.en: What I don't control, what is not up to me, is the outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我无法控制、我力所不及的，是结果。

sentences.en: Sure, I can eat healthy, which I do, largely, and I go regularly to the doctor.
sentences.zh: 当然，我可以吃得健康，我大部分时间也是这么做的，我也会定期去看医生。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, there are a lot of other factors that contribute to the outcome, to the actual
sentences.zh: 然而，还有许多其他因素会影响结果，影响实际的

sentences.en: health, that are not under my control.
sentences.zh: 健康状况，这些是我无法控制的。

sentences.en: I can make all the efforts I want, but to some extent, I am limited by my own genetics
sentences.zh: 我可以尽我所能去努力，但在某种程度上，我受到自身基因的限制

sentences.en: and my own early upbringing.
sentences.zh: 以及我早年的成长环境的影响。

sentences.en: We know that both the genetics and early development, even intrauterine development before you're born and certainly the first few months of development,
sentences.zh: 我们知道，基因和早期发育，甚至是你出生前的宫内发育，当然还有出生后最初几个月的发育，

sentences.en: those are crucial to determine, you know, how you're going to respond long term to certain things.
sentences.zh: 这些对于决定你长期如何应对某些事情至关重要。

sentences.en: And I had no control over those.
sentences.zh: 而我对这些毫无控制力。

sentences.en: I can't rearrange my genes.
sentences.zh: 我无法重组我的基因。

sentences.en: I didn't pick my genes and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我没法选择自己的基因，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So the general idea then becomes that, look, on the one hand, you accept from the get-go the notion that you do not have full control over anything, anything that is external,
sentences.zh: 所以总的思路就变成了，你看，一方面，你要从一开始就接受这样一个观念：你对任何事情都没有完全的控制权，任何外部事物，

sentences.en: none of those things.
sentences.zh: 都不在你的掌控之中。

sentences.en: And you need to be okay with it because what are your choices?
sentences.zh: 你需要坦然接受这一点，因为你还有什么选择呢？

sentences.en: There's only two choices.
sentences.zh: 只有两个选择。

sentences.en: You're either okay with it or you throw a tantrum.
sentences.zh: 要么你坦然接受，要么你大发脾气。

sentences.en: Throwing a tantrum doesn't help.
sentences.zh: 大发脾气无济于事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing that children do because they're not emotionally mature.
sentences.zh: 那是小孩子才会做的事，因为他们情绪还不成熟。

sentences.en: An adult is not supposed to do that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 成年人不应该做那种事。

sentences.en: Also, throwing a tantrum not only doesn't help, but actually gets in the way because
sentences.zh: 而且，大发脾气不仅无济于事，反而会碍事，因为

sentences.en: now you're adding the actual injury from the external to an internal imposed injury.
sentences.zh: 现在你是在外部伤害的基础上，又给自己施加了内在的伤害。

sentences.en: The fact that now you feel bad because you've lost control, you are anxious, and so on
sentences.zh: 因为失去了控制而感到难过、焦虑，诸如此类，

sentences.en: and so forth.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: So you need to focus on what actually you can do, which is empowering because the idea
sentences.zh: 所以你需要专注于你真正能做的事情，这会让你感到更有力量，因为这个观念

sentences.en: is not that you can't do anything about anything.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你对任何事情都无能为力。

sentences.en: You can do quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 你其实能做很多事。

sentences.en: It's just that you need to be very clear on the limits
sentences.zh: 只是你需要非常清楚其中的局限，

sentences.en: and what exactly it is that you can and cannot do.
sentences.zh: 以及你到底能做什么，不能做什么。

sentences.en: And once you are clear on that,
sentences.zh: 一旦你对此有了清晰的认识，

sentences.en: your interventions become much more efficacious
sentences.zh: 你的干预措施就会变得更加有效，

sentences.en: and therefore you feel better.
sentences.zh: 因此你会感觉更好。

sentences.en: And broadly speaking, you get better outcomes.
sentences.zh: 从广义上讲，你也会得到更好的结果。

sentences.en: So Marcus himself followed this advice
sentences.zh: 所以马可·奥勒留本人也遵循了这一建议，

sentences.en: when a terrible plague struck his part of the world.
sentences.zh: 当时一场可怕的瘟疫席卷了他统治的地区。

sentences.en: What happened during this time in the Roman Empire, Massimo,
sentences.zh: 马西莫，在那段时期罗马帝国发生了什么，

sentences.en: and how did Marcus respond to it?
sentences.zh: 马可·奥勒留又是如何应对的？

sentences.en: Yeah, Marcus's reign was made very difficult by a number of issues.
sentences.zh: 是的，马可·奥勒留的统治因一系列问题而变得非常艰难。

sentences.en: One of them is the Antonine Plague, which was the worst plague to hit antiquity.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是安东尼瘟疫，这是古代最严重的瘟疫。

sentences.en: It killed close to 5 million people, and it was probably caused by measles brought back by the legions that were fighting on the east side of the empire.
sentences.zh: 它导致近500万人死亡，很可能是由帝国东部作战的军团带回的麻疹引起的。

sentences.en: He also had to deal with natural disasters, a major flood of the Tiber that devastated Rome, a major earthquake that raised Smyrna in modern Western Turkey.
sentences.zh: 他还必须应对自然灾害，比如台伯河的大洪水摧毁了罗马，以及一场摧毁了现代土耳其西部士麦那的大地震。

sentences.en: So he had a lot of issues to deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以他有很多问题要处理。

sentences.en: Every time he says to himself, okay, what here is up to me and what is not up to me?
sentences.zh: 他每次都会问自己，好吧，这里面什么是我的力所能及，什么是我力所不及的？

sentences.en: For instance, in the case of the plague, the resources of the empire were already depleted by the war.
sentences.zh: 例如，在瘟疫的情况下，帝国的资源已经被战争耗尽了，

sentences.en: against the Parthians.
sentences.zh: 就是针对帕提亚人的战争。

sentences.en: So, you know, even though the Roman Empire was rich,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，尽管罗马帝国很富有，

sentences.en: there is a limit, obviously.
sentences.zh: 但显然也是有限度的。

sentences.en: And so what Marcus thought,
sentences.zh: 所以马可·奥勒留想到的，

sentences.en: one of the things that was up to him
sentences.zh: 他力所能及的事情之一，

sentences.en: was to actually sell a lot of the imperial treasury
sentences.zh: 就是变卖大量的帝国国库资产

sentences.en: and jewels.
sentences.zh: 和珠宝。

sentences.en: So he essentially did auctions
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上举行了拍卖会，

sentences.en: where he sold out a bunch of stuff
sentences.zh: 卖掉了一堆他认为的东西，

sentences.en: that he thought, I don't need this.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，我不需要这些。

sentences.en: This is not making my life better,
sentences.zh: 这些并不能让我的生活变得更好，

sentences.en: but it has the potential to help
sentences.zh: 但它们有潜力帮助

sentences.en: with the relief effort.
sentences.zh: 救灾工作。

sentences.en: And so that's what he did, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他就是这么做的，对吧？

sentences.en: But he was not expecting the plague to just go away, right?
sentences.zh: 但他并没有指望瘟疫会就此消失，对吧？

sentences.en: He said, we don't understand what a plague is
sentences.zh: 他说，我们首先

sentences.en: in the first place.
sentences.zh: 就不了解什么是瘟疫。

sentences.en: We don't know what causes this thing.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是什么导致了这种东西。

sentences.en: We just have to run it out.
sentences.zh: 我们只能熬过去。

sentences.en: We just have to do our best in order to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 我们只能尽我们所能去应对它。

sentences.en: And then it will go away at some point by itself.
sentences.zh: 然后它在某个时候会自然消失。

sentences.en: So this was a situation where Marcus, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个马可·奥勒留，你知道，

sentences.en: wrote in his journal something along the lines of,
sentences.zh: 在他的日记里写下类似这样的话的情况：

sentences.en: what can you do here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里能做什么？

sentences.en: Where can you make a difference?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里可以有所作为？

sentences.en: And just as importantly, he kept repeating to himself that in those areas where he couldn't do anything, it was okay.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，他不断地对自己重复，在那些他无能为力的领域，没关系。

sentences.en: He had to accept that.
sentences.zh: 他必须接受这一点。

sentences.en: This was not something that you want to lose your sleep over because, A, it doesn't help,
sentences.zh: 这不是你应该为此失眠的事情，因为，第一，这无济于事，

sentences.en: and, B, if you lose your sleep over it, then you're actually going to be less efficacious in the kind of things you actually can do.
sentences.zh: 第二，如果你为此失眠，那么你在真正能做的事情上反而会效率更低。

sentences.en: Has this changed the way that you think about your own body image, Massimo?
sentences.zh: 这改变了你对自己身体形象的看法吗，马西莫？

sentences.en: It has.
sentences.zh: 改变了。

sentences.en: I am far less bothered by the issue these days.
sentences.zh: 这些天我被这个问题困扰得少多了。

sentences.en: I focus on what is under my control.
sentences.zh: 我专注于我能控制的事情。

sentences.en: So when I go out for dinner, I try to stay away from things that I know are not good for me.
sentences.zh: 所以当我出去吃饭时，我尽量远离那些我知道对我没好处的东西。

sentences.en: Minimize the damage, as my wife and I call it.
sentences.zh: 正如我和我妻子所说的，尽量减少损害。

sentences.en: And then when I'm home, you know, we have more control, of course, over what we eat.
sentences.zh: 然后当我在家时，你知道，我们当然对吃什么有更多的控制权。

sentences.en: As I said, I go and exercise on a regular basis, and I go to the doctor, and, you know, that's it.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我定期锻炼，去看医生，你知道，就是这样。

sentences.en: But, you know, during the pandemic, for instance,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在疫情期间，例如，

sentences.en: I was reminded one more time that epithelium markers are right because one day I suddenly collapsed the floor and was brought to the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 我再次被提醒，爱比克泰德和马可·奥勒留是对的，因为有一天我突然倒在地板上，被送进了急诊室。

sentences.en: I had absolutely no control over my body, nothing.
sentences.zh: 我对自己身体完全没有控制力，什么都没有。

sentences.en: Turns out to be a rather minor thing.
sentences.zh: 结果发现是一个相当小的问题。

sentences.en: It was a slipped disc and I recovered very quickly and, you know, thanked Zeus for painkillers and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 是椎间盘突出，我恢复得很快，你知道，感谢宙斯赐予止痛药之类的东西。

sentences.en: But that was an instant reminder that, you know, although now it's been years that you exercise, you eat healthy and all that sort of stuff, suddenly you wake up in the morning,
sentences.zh: 但这瞬间提醒了我，你知道，虽然现在你已经锻炼、吃得健康等等好几年了，但突然有一天早上你醒来，

sentences.en: you're about to go out and you collapse on the floor with the very intense feeling that you have no control over your body.
sentences.zh: 正要出门，却倒在地板上，那种你对自己身体毫无控制力的感觉非常强烈。

sentences.en: Okay, what would Epictetus or Marcus have said at this point?
sentences.zh: 好吧，爱比克泰德或马可·奥勒留这时会说什么？

sentences.en: Well, they would say, okay, you just run into one of those externals that is not up to you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们会说，好吧，你只是遇到了那些你力所不及的外部事件之一。

sentences.en: The only thing you can do is to accept it and see what you can do about it in order to recover, to handle the situation, etc.
sentences.zh: 你唯一能做的就是接受它，看看你能做些什么来恢复，来处理这种情况，等等。

sentences.en: I understand that Marcus Aurelius talks at length about the urgency of embracing the present moment,
sentences.zh: 我明白马可·奥勒留详细谈论过拥抱当下的紧迫性，

sentences.en: since none of us ever know how many of those moments we have left.
sentences.zh: 因为我们谁都不知道自己还剩下多少这样的时刻。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea, Massimo.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这个想法吧，马西莫。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When I was young, as a lot of young people, you kind of think that you're immortal.
sentences.zh: 当我年轻的时候，像许多年轻人一样，你会觉得你是永生的。

sentences.en: And that's, of course, not true.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是不对的。

sentences.en: I mean, I have looked up my actual statistics, so to speak, sometime recently, and it turns out that for somebody my age and my ethnic background living in New York,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我最近查过我的实际统计数据，可以这么说，结果发现对于像我这个年龄和族裔背景、住在纽约的人来说，

sentences.en: there is a certain life expectancy.
sentences.zh: 有一定的预期寿命。

sentences.en: And I looked it up and said, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 我查了一下，说，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: So, statistically speaking, I have a couple more decades.
sentences.zh: 所以，从统计学上讲，我还有几十年。

sentences.en: But that's only statistically speaking.
sentences.zh: 但这只是统计学上的说法。

sentences.en: Of course I could die today.
sentences.zh: 当然，我今天就可能死去。

sentences.en: I could cross the street and a car could hit me and that's the end of it.
sentences.zh: 我可能过马路时被车撞了，那就结束了。

sentences.en: Or again, I could contract a lethal disease and I could die.
sentences.zh: 或者，我可能感染了一种致命的疾病，然后死去。

sentences.en: So there is all sorts of stuff that can happen in any time in somebody's life, right?
sentences.zh: 所以一个人一生中随时都可能发生各种各样的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Whether you're young, middle-aged, late, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 无论你是年轻、中年、晚年，等等等等。

sentences.en: And what the Stoics do is they bring that to the forefront of their way of looking at life.
sentences.zh: 斯多葛学派的做法是，把这一点带到他们看待生活方式的最前沿。

sentences.en: um seneca and then marcus constantly say to themselves act as if this was the last day of
sentences.zh: 塞内卡，然后是马可·奥勒留，不断地对自己说：表现得好像这是你生命的最后一天，

sentences.en: your life or if you want to put it more positively you get up in the morning and you realize that
sentences.zh: 或者如果你想更积极地看待它，你早上起床，意识到

sentences.zh: 你又多了一天，耶，庆祝这一天吧，因为你不知道你是否还会

sentences.zh: 以及所有那类事情。

sentences.en: But in fact, they're getting at something fundamental here.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他们触及了一个根本性的东西。

sentences.zh: 让我们的生活变得有意义的观念，

sentences.en: is precisely the fact that it's finite.
sentences.zh: 恰恰在于它是有限的这一事实。

sentences.en: If we actually live forever,
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的能永远活下去，

sentences.en: if you got to do the same things over and over and over ad infinitum,
sentences.zh: 如果你不得不一遍又一遍地做同样的事情，无限循环，

sentences.en: nothing will matter.
sentences.zh: 什么都不会有意义。

sentences.en: Because you always have a remote control
sentences.zh: 因为你总是有遥控器。

sentences.en: that you can rewind and redo it over.
sentences.zh: 你可以倒带重来。

sentences.en: And so it will lose meaning.
sentences.zh: 这样它就会失去意义。

sentences.en: The reality is by focusing, by reminding yourself
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，通过专注，通过提醒自己

sentences.en: that time is in fact finite, and not only that,
sentences.zh: 时间实际上是有限的，不仅如此，

sentences.en: but that you don't know how much you have left,
sentences.zh: 而且你不知道自己还剩下多少时间，

sentences.en: then you need to redouble your efforts to spend the time that you have
sentences.zh: 那么你就需要加倍努力，去度过你拥有的时间，

sentences.en: in a way that it's meaningful, joyous.
sentences.zh: 以一种有意义、快乐的方式。

sentences.en: It's the way you really want to spend your life.
sentences.zh: 这才是你真正想要度过余生的方式。

sentences.en: Think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 换个角度想想。

sentences.en: So you're on a trip somewhere, let's say, near the national parks out west,
sentences.zh: 假设你正在去某个地方旅行，比如去西部国家公园附近，

sentences.en: and you have a car where the gauge for the gas is broken.
sentences.zh: 而你开的车油表坏了。

sentences.en: You don't know how much gas you have.
sentences.zh: 你不知道自己还剩多少油。

sentences.en: You can estimate.
sentences.zh: 你可以估算一下。

sentences.en: You can say, well, I started out with a full tank, you know, three days ago,
sentences.zh: 你可以说，嗯，三天前我加满了油，

sentences.en: so perhaps it's around the end, but you don't know for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以可能快用完了，但你并不确定。

sentences.en: Now, at that point, you need to make very careful decisions about where you're going.
sentences.zh: 那么，在那种情况下，你需要非常谨慎地决定你要去哪里。

sentences.en: You can't just take all sorts of detours for all sorts of reasons or for no reason at all
sentences.zh: 你不能因为各种各样的原因，或者根本没有任何原因就随意绕路，

sentences.en: because you might get stuck in the middle of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 因为你可能会被困在荒郊野外。

sentences.en: You might not get to do what you actually want to do.
sentences.zh: 你可能无法做你真正想做的事情。

sentences.en: This point that Marcus Aurelius is making
sentences.zh: 马可·奥勒留提出的这一点，

sentences.en: was driven home for you, Massimo,
sentences.zh: 对你来说感触很深，马西莫，

sentences.en: when an episode of Brain Fog sent you to the hospital,
sentences.zh: 当一次“脑雾”发作把你送进医院时，

sentences.en: because it's not just the amount of time we have left,
sentences.zh: 因为重要的不仅是我们剩下的时间总量，

sentences.en: but also the amount of good time that we have left.
sentences.zh: 还有我们剩下的美好时光总量。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a very disturbing episode,
sentences.zh: 是的，那是一次非常令人不安的经历，

sentences.en: which thankfully has not repeated itself.
sentences.zh: 好在它没有再发生过。

sentences.en: Basically, I was there trying to write an email to my students,
sentences.zh: 基本上，当时我正试图给学生写一封电子邮件，

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, I realized that my fingers were hitting the keyboard, but I wasn't writing what I thought I was writing.
